renders.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Short words. Concrete images. No jargon, no Sanskrit terms, no meta-commentary.

paragraphs.text: Someone wins and no one can beat him. He is rich in glory, care, wakefulness, and deep joy, and learning lights him up.

People bow to the Lord of the sweet milk-sea. Hate and praise both reach him, and he holds everything. He stays whole though things break. He spans the tiny and the huge. Wise men milk clean knowing out of him and bring him gifts.

renders.prompt: Render the argument of this song in a Gen-Z voice: direct, a little feral, zero cringe, no slang overload. Keep every doctrinal claim intact — voice changes, content does not. No new doctrines, no comparisons, no meta-commentary, no quoted terms.

paragraphs.text: Undefeated and loaded -- glory, care, wakefulness, bliss, plus smarts. Nobody takes his crown.

Milk-ocean boss gets the bow. Your hate mail and fan mail both land on the same desk, and he is holding all of it. Broken world, whole Lord. Ant-sized and cosmos-sized at once. Milk pure knowing out of him and pay up.
